en.name: Napa cabbage
en.summary: Napa cabbage is the tall, pale, loosely packed Chinese cabbage that goes into hotpot, dumpling fillings and kimchi. A whole head keeps 3–5 days wrapped and stood somewhere cool, and 1–2 weeks refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below — though for a napa head, two weeks is optimistic.
en.pantry: A whole head will hold for about 3–5 days out of the fridge if you wrap it in a large sheet of paper and stand it at an angle in a cool, shaded place. Standing rather than lying matters: a head on its side bruises under its own weight and rots where it touches the surface. This works well enough in a cool winter kitchen and badly in a humid summer one, and the fridge is the better option whenever you have the space.
en.fridge: Refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in the crisper or a moisture-resistant wrap, napa cabbage keeps 1–2 weeks from purchase. Keep the head whole and peel leaves off as you need them rather than cutting it in half — a cut face browns, dries and then goes slimy, while an intact head simply loses its outermost leaf. Bear in mind the published figure covers cabbage generally: napa is looser-leaved and much softer than a dense green head cabbage, so treat two weeks as the optimistic end rather than the expectation.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for napa cabbage in our sources, so we are not giving one. Raw, it is far too watery to freeze well — it thaws limp and floods whatever you put it in. The traditional solutions are better: salt it and make kimchi, which is a storage method in its own right, or blanch and squeeze it hard before it goes into a bag, which at least makes a usable dumpling filling later.
spoilage: Slimy, blackened or translucent outer leaves
Brown or grey spots spreading across the white ribs
A soft, wet, foul-smelling core at the base
A sour or strongly sulphurous smell when the head is cut
tips: Choose a head that feels heavy and tightly packed with crisp white ribs.
Store it whole and standing up; peel leaves off from the outside.
Small black specks on the ribs are usually a harmless pigment disorder, not mould — rinse and use.
Cook the thick white ribs first and add the leafy tops at the end.

faq.q: How long does napa cabbage last in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 weeks from the day of purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept whole in the crisper. Because napa is softer than green cabbage, treat two weeks as the optimistic end.
Not immediately. Wrapped in paper and stood at an angle somewhere cool it keeps 3–5 days, but the fridge roughly triples that.
No published timeline exists, so we do not give one. It is too watery to freeze raw; salting it into kimchi, or blanching and squeezing it dry, are better ways to keep it.

faq.q: What are the little black dots on the leaves?
faq.a: Usually pepper spot, a harmless physiological disorder caused by growing conditions or long cold storage. It looks unappetising but the cabbage is fine to eat.

zh.name: 大白菜
zh.summary: 大白菜就是火鍋、水餃餡和泡菜裡不可或缺的那顆高身、淡色、葉片鬆散的結球白菜。整顆包好立放在陰涼處可放 3～5 天；4°C 以下冷藏，從購買當天算起 1～2 週——不過對大白菜來說，兩週算是相當樂觀。
zh.pantry: 整顆大白菜用大張紙包起來、斜立在陰涼避光處，大約可以放 3～5 天。立著而不是躺著很重要：橫放的菜會被自身重量壓傷，接觸面最先爛掉。這個做法在涼爽的冬天廚房沒問題，在悶熱潮濕的夏天就不太行；只要冰箱放得下，冷藏都是更好的選擇。
zh.fridge: 放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，或用能擋水氣的材質包好，從購買日起可放 1～2 週。請保持整顆完整，要用時從外層一片片剝，不要整顆對切——切面會褐變、乾掉，然後開始變黏；完整的菜球頂多是外層那片葉子壞掉。另外要注意，公布的數字涵蓋的是「高麗菜、白菜類」整體，而大白菜葉片鬆散、質地也比結球高麗菜柔軟得多，所以兩週請當成樂觀上限，而不是預期值。
zh.freezer: 我們的資料來源中沒有大白菜的冷凍保存期限，因此不提供。生的大白菜含水量太高，根本不適合直接冷凍——解凍後軟爛出水，會把整鍋菜稀釋掉。傳統做法反而更好：抹鹽做成泡菜，本身就是一種保存法；或是先汆燙、用力擠乾再裝袋，至少之後還能拿來包水餃。
spoilage: 外層葉子黏滑、發黑或變得半透明
白色葉梗上出現褐色或灰色斑塊並擴散
根部菜心變軟濕爛並發出臭味
切開時聞到酸味或濃重的硫磺味
tips: 挑拿起來有重量、包得紮實、葉梗白脆的。
整顆保存並立著放，要用時從外層剝。
葉梗上的小黑點多半是無害的生理性斑點而非發霉，沖洗後照常使用。
料理時先下厚厚的白色菜梗，葉子最後再放。

faq.q: 大白菜放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、整顆放在蔬果保鮮室，從購買當天算起 1～2 週。大白菜比高麗菜軟，兩週請當成樂觀上限。
不一定要馬上冷藏。用紙包好、斜立在陰涼處可以放 3～5 天，但冷藏大約能延長到三倍。
沒有公布的冷凍期限，所以我們不給數字。生的太多水不適合直接冷凍；做成泡菜，或汆燙擠乾後再冷凍，都是更好的做法。

faq.q: 葉子上的小黑點是什麼？
faq.a: 多半是「芝麻點」，由生長環境或長期低溫貯藏造成的生理性斑點，無害。外觀不好看，但可以正常食用。
